title: danthonia raoulii
intro: Danthonia raoulii, commonly known as Raoul's grass, is a species of grass native to New Zealand. It has been used in traditional Maori medicine for its potential health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, promoting wound healing, and acting as an antiseptic agent. The bioactive constituents of Danthonia raoulii include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and sesquiterpenes, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. Further research is needed to fully understand the health benefits and therapeutic actions of Raoul's grass, but it has been traditionally used to treat various conditions, including skin irritations and respiratory issues.
